summary: Clarifies how IPv6 addresses are written in the Session Description Protocol. It was replaced by RFC 4566.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 3266 clarifies how IPv6 addresses are written in SDP, a text format for describing multimedia sessions. It defines address syntax and permits the IP6 address type in a connection field; RFC 4566 later obsoleted it.

questions: how do you write ipv6 addresses in sdp
what is the ip6 address type in sdp
how should sdp handle ipv4 mapped ipv6 addresses
subtitle: Clarifies the syntax for IPv6 addresses in Session Description Protocol text.

tldr.problem: SDP left IPv6 address syntax undefined even though session descriptions can contain IPv6 addresses.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC updates SDP's ABNF to use the IPv6 text formats defined by the referenced address specifications and allows the IP6 address type in the connection field.
tldr.outcome: RFC 3266 updates RFC 2327 and was obsoleted by RFC 4566.

sections.title: Why SDP Needed IPv6 Syntax
sections.content:
Session Description Protocol (SDP) describes multimedia sessions, including origin information, connection addresses for media, and optional attributes. These fields may involve IPv6 addresses, but the existing ABNF for IP addresses did not define their syntax.

RFC 3266 updates RFC 2327 to complete that syntax and clarify that the address type IP6 is allowed in the SDP connection field, c=.
sections.plainLanguage: SDP could describe IPv4 addresses but did not say how to write IPv6 addresses. This memo fills in that missing rule.

sections.title: IPv6 Address Forms in SDP
sections.content:
The RFC uses the textual IPv6 address syntax from RFC 2373 and the URL representation rules from RFC 2732. Its ABNF allows IPv6 unicast addresses in the address field and IPv6 multicast addresses in the multicast-address field. The IP6 address type identifies an IPv6 address.

The example session description uses IPv6 addresses in the origin and connection fields. The RFC warns implementers to treat an IPv4-mapped IPv6 address as equivalent to an IP4 address because it is the address of an IPv4-only node.
sections.plainLanguage: SDP uses the defined text form of IPv6 addresses. An IPv4-mapped address still represents an IPv4-only node and should be handled as IP4.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content: The RFC says there are no additional security considerations beyond those stated in RFC 2327. RFC 3266 updates the definition of the IP6 address-type parameter and was later obsoleted by RFC 4566.
sections.plainLanguage: The memo adds no security considerations beyond the underlying SDP specification. RFC 4566 later replaced it.
